messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call. Multiple GPU driver reset (Xid) alerts from cluster 'infer-prod' - affected nodes: gpu-node-17, gpu-node-18, gpu-node-20. Error rate spike at 2309876500 UTC. See metrics: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/infer-cluster

alex: on it. pinging SRE-Lead. I can start triage on gpu-node-17.

Priya: @alex @SRE-Lead any customer impact so far? are requests failing or just retries?

Jamie: seeing elevated 5xx on /v1/generate on region-us-west. 4.7% error rate in last 5m, p95 latency up from 120ms to 720ms.

Morgan: quick check - autoscaler is healthy. A lot of pods are restarting on those nodes (OOM and crashloop).

alex: grabbing node logs now. dmesg shows repeated "NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus" and Xid 79/43 messages. suspect driver reset. snippet: ```
[ 3421.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3a:00): 79, PID=4212 
[ 3421.123457] NVRM: GPU at 00000000:3a:00: GPU has fallen off the bus.````

SRE-Lead: ok, plan: 1) cordon gpu-node-17/18/20 2) evict long-running inference pods to alternative nodes 3) enable fallback routing to cpu/quantized model for user-facing routes 4) open customer bridge if impact > 5% error. Alex/Morgan do cordon+drain. Priya monitor customer impact and decide bridge. Jamie follow metrics.

alex: cordoned gpu-node-17, starting drain for inference pods. command: ```kubectl cordon gpu-node-17 && kubectl drain gpu-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=30```

Morgan: started moving pods. noticed some pods stuck Terminating due to oom-kill in container logs. example: ```OOMKilled process pid=9876 name=python3 mem=18G```

Jamie: posting current error breakdown: 
- gpu-node-17: 63 restarts last 10m
- gpu-node-18: 47 restarts last 10m
- gpu-node-20: 9 restarts last 10m
- overall 5xx spike corresponds to those nodes.

Priya: customers: two production customers seeing increased error rate. Support updated them with initial note. If this crosses 10% errors I'll open the bridge.

support-agent: sent targeted message to affected customers (IDs masked) linking status page and temporary mitigation steps. :white_check_mark:

Morgan: triggered fallback routing for route /v1/generate to model-id:redwood-tiny-cpu for new sessions in us-west. This reduces quality but keeps availability. Patch applied via routing policy: ```PATCH /routing/policy/regions/us-west {"fallback_model":"redwood-tiny-cpu","duration":15m}```

Priya: doing real-time customer monitoring. so far errors dropped from 4.7% -> 1.8% after partial evac + fallback. still seeing retries from sessions that were mid-request.

alex: gpu-node-18 cordoned and drained. gpu-node-20 showing similar Xid messages but lower rate. I've isolated one pod that repeatedly causes OOM on startup - moving to smaller batch config.

SRE-Lead: good. next, check firmware/drivers timeline. any recent driver upgrades? Jamie?

Jamie: no driver change in last 72h. but we pushed a new model container yesterday with slightly larger initial KV cache allocation. possible mem pressure pattern. logs show repeated kernel oops around gpu memory allocation.

alex: collected `nvidia-smi` snapshots before reset: memory usage climbing to 99% and process list shows several stale python processes holding GPU memory after container restart. suspect leak in model binary.

SRE-Lead: emergency decision: keep fallback routing for 30m, leave cordoned nodes offline for now. escalate to infra-hardware to run vendor diagnostics (ECC checks). open a hardware ticket. Priya please open customer bridge as precaution (>=2 affected customers).

Priya: opening bridge now. customer-bridge-bot: Bridge created: https://zoom.bridge/abc-incident-2309876543. Participants: infra, SRE, support, oncall. :telephone_receiver:

support-agent: posted status update to customers and status page: "We are investigating GPU driver resets affecting a subset of nodes in US-West. We have enabled fallback routing to maintain availability; some degradation possible."

Morgan: also rolled an autoscale policy tweak to avoid scheduling large-batch pods onto remaining GPUs for 20m: ```kubectl apply -f autoscale-patch.yaml```

alex: forensics note - kernel log also shows ECC error counters rising on gpu-node-17 prior to resets. snippet: ```ECC single-bit corrected errors: 1240```

SRE-Lead: that leans toward hardware/ECC issue not purely software. infra-hardware: please prioritize. Meanwhile keep fallbacks and small-batch queue.

Jamie: metrics show error rate stabilized ~1.2% now, latency p95 back to ~200ms for routed traffic. Noticed a small uptick in CPU-backed request latency (expected).

Priya: on the bridge, customer asked for ETA. we told them initial mitigation in place, hardware diag queued. they want an RCA within 48h. logging that.

incident-bot: runbook link: https://wiki.redwood/internal/runbooks/gpu-driver-reset - step 4 suggests ECC evaluation and hardware swap if ECC counters > 1k in 24h.

Morgan: starting to repro the crash in staging with the same model container and batch config. initial result: memory leak confirmed after long-running sequence generation. filing bug against inference runtime.

alex: marking gpu-node-17/18/20 as maintenance-mode for now. created ticket HW-9876 for vendor swap.

SRE-Lead: summary so far: cause likely combination of increased model KV allocation + hardware ECC degradation triggering driver resets -> OOMs -> container restarts -> customer impact. Actions: fallback routing in place, nodes cordoned, hardware ticket open, bug filed for runtime memory leak, status updates to customers, post-incident RCA planned.

Priya: updating incident tracker with timeline and customer comms. will keep bridge open until nodes back in service or for 4 hours.

support-agent: customers acknowledged mitigation and appreciate transparency. one asked for temporary quota increase to shift load away from affected region - approved.

SRE-Lead: any outstanding work? Morgan to continue repro and patch runtime, infra to replace suspected GPU(s), Alex coordinate node revalidation. If nodes pass ECC and vendor tests we'll uncordon cautiously with canary traffic and revert fallback routing.

Jamie: will run a canary release with 2 pods on one repaired node and monitor for 30m before full rejoin. alert thresholds tightened during canary.

Priya: agreed. bridge will remain open until at least 2309877120 UTC or until nodes stable.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident logged ID INC-2309876543. Reminder: file postmortem in /postmortems/incidents within 72h.

SRE-Lead: thanks team. good coordination. I'll lead the RCA. closing this thread for operational chatter; leave bridge for action items. :thumbsup:
